about.title: Rancho Cordova Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Most drivers in Rancho Cordova know the rhythm of Sunrise Boulevard at the end of a workday, or how Folsom Boulevard and Coloma Road fill up once offices let out. In 2025, public records for this Sacramento County city show 292 injury collisions, 426 people hurt, and 9 traffic deaths. Thursday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. account for a noticeable share of those reports, and Sunrise Boulevard, Zinfandel Drive, Coloma Road and Folsom Boulevard appear most often in the collision counts. Behind each figure is a person dealing with a car that will not start, a neck that stiffens overnight, and an adjuster who calls before the tow bill even arrives. LawProactive exists for that moment. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that matches you with an independent California personal injury attorney who takes car accident cases on contingency, meaning you owe nothing unless there is a recovery. You concentrate on getting better while the attorney sorts out liability, medical bills and the insurance back-and-forth.

whyChoose.title: Why Rancho Cordova Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines Are Shorter Than They Look
items.desc: California gives most car accident victims two years to file, but if a city, county or state vehicle was involved, a written claim may be due in as little as six months. An early connection with an attorney keeps those dates from slipping past.

items.title: Partial Fault Does Not End Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you share some blame; your compensation is simply reduced by your percentage. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your share.

items.title: No Cap, No Upfront Fee, No Recorded Statement
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost quality of life, and network attorneys work on contingency. They will also handle the other driver's insurer so you are not pressured into a recorded statement that can be used against you.

items.question: I was rear-ended near Zinfandel Drive and Folsom Boulevard. What should I do in the first few days?
items.answer: Get checked by a doctor even if you feel mostly fine, because neck and back symptoms often surface a day or two later. Photograph your vehicle, the scene and any visible injuries, and request the collision report from the responding agency. Politely decline to give the other driver's insurer a recorded statement until you have spoken with an attorney.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company keeps calling me. Do I have to talk to them?
items.answer: You are not required to give the other side's adjuster a recorded statement, and it is usually wise not to. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that minimize the claim, and an offhand remark about feeling okay can be quoted later. Once you are connected with an attorney, that attorney can handle all communication for you.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a car accident claim in Rancho Cordova?
items.answer: For most crashes in California, the statute of limitations is two years from the date of injury. If a government vehicle or a public roadway defect is part of the picture, a formal claim may need to be filed within six months. Because evidence such as camera footage and witness memories fades quickly, starting sooner protects your options.
